patients.summary: Construction laborer with severe alcohol use disorder who joined in 2021 with alcoholic liver disease, then developed chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency, alcoholic cerebellar degeneration and thiamine deficiency, was treated for tuberculous spondylitis, and has had alcoholic hepatitis, withdrawal, delirium tremens and withdrawal seizures. Lives with his brother; outside records arrive late or not at all.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking for a primary doctor; has not had one since moving to the area. Has MassHealth, confirmed we take his plan. Works construction, days vary, prefers early mornings. New patient visit booked 9/14 at 8:00. Asked him to bring any pill bottles and any old records he has. Says he doesn't have any.

conditions.label: Alcohol use disorder, severe
conditions.note: about 6 beers daily for 20 years; prior withdrawal episodes by report

orders.reason: elevated liver enzymes, heavy alcohol use

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
49M establishing care. No PCP since moving to the US in 2019; before that, care was sporadic and he has no records to send. Works construction (laborer, mostly framing and demo).

Alcohol: up front about it. Drinks about 6 beers a day, has for roughly 20 years. Has been through withdrawal before, several times, treated in EDs; can't give dates. Longest dry spells 1 to 3 months, then back to it. Not interested in a program today but willing to keep talking.
Tobacco: smokes, about a pack a day on and off since his late 20s. Thinking about quitting.
No drugs.

PMH: nothing he knows of. PSH: none. Meds: none. NKDA.
FH: father had alcohol use disorder and died with cirrhosis. Mother type 2 diabetes. Brother has high blood pressure; he lives with his brother and his brother's family.

ROS: appetite fair, no abdominal pain, no jaundice he's noticed, no GI bleeding. No chest pain or dyspnea.

Exam: thin man, NAD. Anicteric. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver edge not palpable, no ascites. No spider angiomata. No tremor today. Gait normal.

AUDIT-C 10. PHQ-9 5.

A/P
1. Severe alcohol use disorder. Long talk. Not ready to cut back much; agreed to come back in a few months. Gave him the outpatient addiction services list. Start thiamine 100 daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, multivitamin.
2. Liver: check CMP, CBC, GGT; hep C and hep B serologies; RUQ ultrasound.
3. Tobacco: advised quitting, he'll think about it.
4. Health maintenance: flu shot next month with RN. Colorectal screening due, FIT at that visit.

documents.title: Your blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rohan, your liver tests are up: AST 68, ALT 47 and GGT 290. That pattern fits alcohol affecting the liver. Liver function itself (bilirubin, albumin) is OK, and your blood counts are fine. Hepatitis C test is negative. Your hepatitis B tests show you have never had it and are not immune, so I'd like to vaccinate you; we can start that at a follow-up. The ultrasound is scheduled for 9/28.

reports.text:
Indication: elevated transaminases, heavy alcohol use.
Technique: grayscale and color Doppler sonography of the right upper quadrant.
Liver: normal in size. Diffusely increased echogenicity with mild attenuation of the sound beam. No focal lesion. Hepatic contour smooth.
Gallbladder: normal wall, no stones, no pericholecystic fluid. Sonographic Murphy sign negative.
Bile ducts: no intrahepatic ductal dilatation. Common duct 4 mm.
Portal vein: patent with normal hepatopetal flow.
Pancreas: head and body unremarkable where seen; tail obscured by bowel gas.
Right kidney: normal size, no hydronephrosis.
Spleen: normal in size.
No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Diffusely echogenic liver consistent with hepatic steatosis. No focal liver lesion. No biliary dilatation.

documents.title: Result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Steatosis on US, nothing focal, spleen normal size. With the enzyme pattern and his intake this is alcoholic liver disease. Added to problem list. RN to call.

documents.title: Result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Reached pt on his lunch break. Reviewed US: fatty liver from alcohol, no masses, no scarring seen on this test. Explained cutting down is what lets the liver recover. He said "I know." Confirmed nurse visit 10/19 for flu shot. Taking the vitamins.

documents.title: Nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, tolerated. FIT kit given with instructions, he'll mail it from work. Reminded him of follow-up with PCP in December.

documents.title: Result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in one year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for follow-up. Drinking about the same, 5 or 6 a night after work. Says he tried to skip weekends in November and made it one weekend. Still smoking. Taking the vitamins most days. No abdominal pain, no yellowing. Work is slow for winter.
O: Vitals as charted. Anicteric. Abdomen soft, nontender. No tremor.
A/P: AUD, severe, precontemplative to contemplative. Talked about what a first step could look like; he'd like to try cutting to weekdays only. Not interested in medication or a program right now, which I respect, and the door stays open. ALD: repeat LFTs today. Tobacco: discussed, would like to quit after the holidays. Tdap today. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for thiamine and folic acid, 90-day supply. Last seen 12/7. Pended for PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Good news first: stopped smoking the second week of January, cold turkey, and has not had one since. About 20 pack-years. Proud of it, as he should be.
Alcohol: weekdays-only didn't stick. Still most nights, maybe a bit less. AUDIT-C 9.
No GI complaints. Weight down a little from fall.
Exam: well appearing, anicteric, abdomen benign.
Plan: congratulated on quitting, reviewed triggers. Alcohol: same conversation, same answer; continue vitamins. PCV20 given for alcohol use disorder and smoking history. Hep B series dose 1 today, RN for dose 2 in a month and dose 3 in the fall. Labs at next visit. RTC 3 to 4 months.

documents.title: Nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep B dose 2 IM R deltoid. No reaction to dose 1. Dose 3 due in September or later; will pair with flu shot.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Missed June, says a job ran long. Busy season, out on a site six days a week. Still not smoking.
Drinking unchanged. Eating less in the heat. Stools have been a bit looser the last month or so, figures it's the beer. No blood, no pain.
Weight 59, down 2 kg since last fall.
Exam: thin, anicteric, abdomen soft and nontender. No tremor.
A/P: AUD severe, ALD: labs today. Weight trending down; asked him to eat a real breakfast and lunch and we'll recheck. If stools stay loose, tell us. Hep B #3 and flu shot in October. RTC fall.

documents.title: Nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hep B dose 3 (series complete), flu and COVID bivalent booster given, split arms. Waited 15 min, fine. New FIT kit handed over; last year's was negative. Pt asked to reschedule his PCP follow-up to December when work slows.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: weight loss, loose stools.

HPI: About six months now of loose stools that he describes as big, greasy and smelling terrible, hard to flush. Several a day. Over the same stretch he has lost weight without trying; down to 55 kg from 61 at his first visit here. Also gets episodes of pain high in the belly that bores through to his back, worse after a big meal. No vomiting, no black or bloody stools, no fevers.
Alcohol: stopped drinking at the start of December after a bad weekend, about ten days dry so far. No shakes this time.
FIT kit from October not returned.

Exam: thin, temporal wasting. Anicteric today. Abdomen soft, tender in the epigastrium, no rebound, no guarding, no mass. No edema.

A/P
1. Weight loss with steatorrhea and epigastric pain radiating to the back in a long-term heavy drinker: concerning for chronic pancreatitis with malabsorption. Referring to GI, asked for the soonest slot. CMP and CBC today.
2. AUD: newly abstinent. Encouraged; reviewed withdrawal warning signs and to go to the ED for confusion, shaking or seizures if he drinks and stops again.
3. Continue thiamine, folate, MVI.

documents.title: Referral scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: GI office has him on 1/5 at 10:30. Called pt, gave date and address. He'll get a ride from his brother.
